title: What does music say about the world?
text: Popular music offers a lens into cultural moments, social shifts, and technological revolutions. By tracking which genres dominated the Billboard charts over seven decades, we can see how American musical tastes have transformed over time.

title: Music Mapped: Regional Sounds Across America
text:
Music in America has always had a sense of place. Long before streaming and algorithms put every song in everyone’s pocket, where you lived shaped what came out of your speakers. Detroit ran on Motown soul, Austin and Nashville lived on country storytelling, California was soundtracked by surf and psychedelic rock, and New York block parties gave birth to hip-hop.
Hit the decade buttons below to see how America’s regional tastes shifted over the last 60 years. Click on any state to see its most popular sound, signature artists, and the local music scene that defined it.

title: Music Mapped: Regional Sounds Across America
section: How America’s Soundtrack Moved Across Decades
text:
How America’s Soundtrack Moved Across Decades


📻 The 60s & 70s: When Cities Built the Sounds
California owned youth culture with sunny surf rock and Laurel Canyon counterculture, while Berry Gordy’s Motown headquarters in Detroit churned out timeless soul with Stevie Wonder and The Supremes. Down South, Nashville and Texas dug deep into honky-tonk and outlaw country with Johnny Cash and Willie Nelson.


📺 The 80s & 90s: From NYC Block Parties to Seattle Basements
In the 1980s, New York City park jams and turntables ignited the golden era of hip-hop. Fast forward to the 1990s, and the rainy Pacific Northwest caught fire when Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Soundgarden pushed raw grunge out of local clubs and onto MTV, changing rock forever.


💿 The 2000s & 2010s: The South Takes the Crown
Atlanta became the undisputed heavyweight of American music. Between Outkast, Ludacris, and later Future and Migos, southern trap and melodic rap became the dominant sound on car stereos and headphones across the country. Meanwhile, stadium country expanded far outside the South into heartland arenas.


📱 The 2020s: Viral Waves and Big Comebacks
Today, anyone with a phone and a catchy chorus can blow up nationwide overnight. But regional pride is still huge: country stars like Morgan Wallen and Zach Bryan are breaking all-time streaming records, while pop superstars like Taylor Swift sell out stadiums from coast to coast.

title: Genre Influences & Lineage
text:

title: Genre Influences & Lineage
section: The DNA of America’s 6 Billboard Super-Genres
text:
The DNA of America’s 6 Billboard Super-Genres


💖 Pop (1,700 Hits)

Primary Influences: Dance-pop, Motown melodies, Hip-Hop beats, and Rock hooks.
The Story: Pop is a musical sponge. Rather than existing in isolation, pop takes the catchiest elements of whatever genres are currently popular—from 80s disco synths to 2010s EDM drops and rap verses.



🎸 Rock (1,646 Hits)

Primary Influences: Delta Blues, Early Rock & Roll, and Appalachian Folk.
The Story: Electrifying the acoustic blues and 12-bar chord progressions of the 1940s created the guitar-driven sound that dominated the Billboard Hot 100 for four straight decades.



🎤 Hip-Hop/Rap (1,172 Hits)

Primary Influences: 70s Funk drum breaks, Disco basslines, and spoken-word storytelling.
The Story: Born on Bronx park turntables by isolating funk drum breaks, hip-hop evolved through 90s lyricism to become the single most dominant streaming genre today.



💜 R&B/Soul (917 Hits)

Primary Influences: Church Gospel vocal arrangements, Delta Blues, and Motown harmony.
The Story: Soul and R&B translated the raw passion and call-and-response of gospel music into secular chart hits, pioneering the vocal acrobatics heard across modern pop and soul.



🤠 Country (597 Hits)

Primary Influences: Appalachian Folk, Bluegrass, Western Swing, and Honky-Tonk.
The Story: Rooted in acoustic balladry and storytelling, country expanded from regional radio barn dances into stadium-filling crossover hits with rock guitars and pop hooks.



⚡ Electronic/Dance (668 Hits)

Primary Influences: German synthesizers (Kraftwerk), 70s Disco, Chicago House, and Detroit Techno.
The Story: Electronic music swapped acoustic drums and guitars for synthesizers and sequencers, moving from underground clubs into global festival anthems.
